item.title: What a federal plan to reallocate the Colorado River's water means for western states
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Russ Schumacher, professor at Colorado State University, about a new government proposal to reallocate water from the Colorado River among Western states who rely on it.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Russ Schumacher, professor at Colorado State University, about a new government proposal to reallocate water from the Colorado River among Western states who rely on it.
item.dc:creator: Rob Schmitz

item.title: A new federal plan to manage the Colorado river faces a possible future of water cuts
item.description: Under a new federal plan out today to manage the Colorado river, Arizona, California and Nevada face potentially steep water cuts over the next decade. The plan by the Interior Department will impact communities and farms across those states. For now, the proposal spares Colorado, Utah, New Mexico and Wyoming from mandatory water cuts. Legal battles are expected.

item.title: 50 years after landmark laws, some U.S. rivers are recovering but threats remain
item.description: Half a century ago, a series of landmark federal laws started reining in water pollution. As a result, some rivers across the country are bouncing back to life, but threats to clean rivers remain.

item.title: In France and Spain, the battle to contain wildfires faces another heatwave
item.description: Authorities in France and Spain say some of their wildfires are mostly contained, but others are blazing on and a new wave of extreme heat is raising fears of more fires to come.

item.title: Death toll rises to 18 as rescuers comb through quake rubble in southwestern Japan
item.description: Soldiers and emergency workers combed through a badly damaged shopping mall and collapsed houses looking for trapped survivors Wednesday after a powerful earthquake that killed at least 18 people, including a foreigner, in southwestern Japan.

item.title: Kill your lawn, plant native flowers
item.description: Traditional lawns may be green, but that doesn't mean they're good for the environment. The team at NPR's Life Kit podcast report on one lawn alternative that's gaining popularity.

item.title: France continues to fight devastating wildfires, while progress is made in Spain
item.description: In southern France, a wildfire in the region of Gironde is still active, while two major fires in central Spain are finally coming under control, ahead of the fourth heat wave of the summer.

item.title: Climate change is now threatening a pillar of childhood: summer break
item.description: When summer rolls around, many parents scramble to sign up their young kids for outdoor activities. But what do you do when extreme heat and wildfire smoke increasingly make the outdoors dangerous?

item.title: A strange transmissible cancer is spreading through the catfish in this lake
item.description: For more than a decade, there's been something fishy going on in a lake that straddles Vermont and the province of Quebec. It involves cancer, a kind of catfish, and — possibly — clues about how tumors metastasize.
